news.title: Number of children requiring special education placements is 'evolving all the time', says minister
news.text:
The department’s budget for 2027 includes funding for 1,352 special education teachers and 2,339 special needs assistants (SNAs) under a €3.8bn allocation to special education.

Separately, the Department of Education figures put the number of children receiving support for special educational needs now at 250,000, growing from 70,000 a decade ago. 

 To receive a special educational placement, either in a special class or special school, parents must register through the Parents Notify portal, run by the National Council for Special Education (NCSE). This year, the deadline to apply for 2027 was brought forward to the end of September.

Announcing the move over the summer, Ms Naughton said it was necessary to give her “the opportunity to feed into the budgetary process to meet the needs of the most vulnerable children in our society”. 

On Wednesday, neither Ms Naughton or Mr Moynihan would provide the figure their department put forward during budget negotiations.

Ms Naughton said: "As part of our budget negotiations, it was really important that we can, number one, forward plan, and having the portal in place is a really critical part of that." 

The numbers for 2027 are coming in “the whole time”, she said.

“We are confident that we have the budget for September in 2027 in relation to the demand for special education.” She added: “These figures are evolving all the time.” 

Bringing the portal deadline back gave the department greater insight around forward planning, said Mr Moynihan.

The October deadline last year was not a “cliff edge” deadline because numbers kept coming in, Mr. Moynihan added. “And we are still accepting numbers after September 1 [this year].” 

He added: “It is wrong to give a number because that would give an impression to families ‘well, that’s the number now, that’s all they are doing’.” 

He urged families who need access to special education for 2027 to continue to use the Parents Notify portal.

“We have sight on what we need to do but those numbers will change right up to next year because students within schools, parents will want to try mainstream schools, maybe it doesn’t work out. We are engaging. The NCSE, ourselves, and the department are meeting on a weekly basis to review and to ensure we’ve sight on where the challenges are.

"But that number will change, and if I give you a number today, that number would not be accurate in two weeks time, or even two days time.” 

 Jess Casey is Education Correspondent.
news.summary: The Department of Education figures put the number of children receiving support for special educational needs now at 250,000, growing from 70,000 a decade ago

news.title: Patients and consultants take case for stem cell transplant unit in Cork to Leinster House
news.text:
The unit closed temporarily almost 20 years ago. Now transplant patients in Munster hospitals are transferred to Galway or St James hospital in Dublin for the procedure.

Musician Mags McCarthy started the campaign, motivated by watching her own father travel to Dublin from Cork for care.

“We’re doing a presentation to get everybody on board, and hopefully prioritise a transplant centre for Cork.

“That would help all patients as there is no stem cell transplantation in the south of Ireland now,” she said before the meeting.

Former patient Denis O’Donovan travelled from Blarney to support the campaign following his experiences in 2021.

“I had to get treated in St James so it meant commuting up and down to Dublin which is so inconvenient,” he said.

“We had to get up at 5.30am to get the 7am train to get up to get my bloods done at 9.30am.” 

He only lives about 20 minutes from Cork University Hospital, he added.

Another former patient Noel Casey made three trips to Galway, including once by ambulance back to Cork. 

“Your immune system is gone so you’re very isolated. It was covid time so if you got covid you were a goner. Galway were very good to us, but it’s just the travelling.” 

Medical experts attending included Vitaliy Mykytiv, clinical director of diagnosis and therapeutics at CUH.

Also present was president of the European Society for Blood and Marrow Transplantation professor Ibrahim Yakoub-Agha.

The ratio between transplant centres and population numbers in Ireland is “really below the European range”, he said.

He described how two hours is the maximum travel time recommended between patients’ homes and transplant centres.

“Even two hours is a really long time because if you go to see a specialist that is four hours travelling for very tired patients,” he said.

“When we calculate in Ireland you have only one allogeneic stem cell transplant centre in Dublin. So for patients from the south of Ireland the distance is something like three hours. It’s a red flag because it’s a very long distance.” 

Prof. Yakoub-Agha also said medical students at University College Cork should be exposed to the most advanced treatments available.

The meeting was arranged by Fine Gael senator Eileen Lynch.

“There’s over 2,400 people here in Ireland diagnosed with a blood cancer, but currently you can only have a stem cell transplant in Galway and Dublin while you can get pre-care and aftercare in CUH,” she said.

She called for investment through the capital budget for health in the unit.
news.summary: At the moment, transplant patients in Munster hospitals are transferred to Galway or St James hospital in Dublin for the procedure

news.title: Mary McAleese integration  replacement unveiled on Friday
news.text:
Meetings have been called for as early as Thursday evening and the Irish Examiner understands the individual is a man.

“We met as a group on Monday,” said GAA director general Tom Ryan, replying to a question from Fianna Fáil TD for Wexford-Wicklow Malcolm Byrne. “We agreed unanimously on a nominee for that position and that person has agreed to take up that role.

“There’s a small process to be undertaken in each of the three organisations. Each organisation over the course of the next, I want to say, 24 hours will be meeting to formally ratify, appoint that person. We’ll be making that announcement very shortly.” 

Asked by Fine Gael TD Wexford-Wicklow Brian Brennan why he felt McAleese stepped down as SGI chairperson, GAA president Jarlath Burns suggested she did not accept the first deadline of 2027 would not be achieved.

“I think she resigned because she was very adamant that we would reach every deadline that we had, and once she realised we were going to miss the first deadline, I think she decided then that she wanted to walk away from the process, which was very disappointing for us and we regret that deeply.

“But we are still very much committed to integration. We really do want to make it happen and it’s up to us – we will make it happen – but we will make it happen in a way that our numbers are comfortable with and will vote for.” 

There was a reluctance on the part of the Gaelic bodies to provide new timelines in the wake of last month’s confirmation that next year’s deadline will not be met.

LGFA chief executive Lyn Savage said it was “a brave decision” to postpone the deadline of 2027, insisting “we needed to get it right”. She rejected the suggestion it was a failure.

In a response to a question from Sinn Féin TD for Dublin South-Central Aengus Ó Snodaigh about a date for full integration, GAA director general Tom Ryan was happy to say it would take “years”.

Labour TD for Tipperary North and joint-committee chairperson Alan Kelly said the Gaelic bodies would be invited to meet the deputies and senators again in December where he said he and his colleagues "will need to know" the revised timeplan.

In a press release last month, The Camogie Association president Brian Molloy said January 2028 as “the new “delivery date for the GAA to become the single NGB (national governing body) for all Gaelic Games”.

Burns said there had been disquiet among some in the LGFA and The Camogie Association about the structure proposed structure of vice-presidents working under one president. “That was taken by some people to be the GAA are getting the presidency and the poor LGFA and The Camogie Association are only getting the vice-presidents.” 

He admitted he and Molloy had different opinions on how the integration process should proceed. “I think we’re better going incrementally. Brian and I discuss this all the time. Brian feels we should start off with structures and then do the rest at a second Congress.

“I think incrementally is better, start off with structures, and even if we say ‘these are the structures we’re aspirationally going to have’ then all of the county implementation committees can do some meaningful work.

“We have actually found it very hard to get those (committees) into action because they’re saying to us, ‘What are we getting ready for?’”

Burns outlined some of the work the GAA already does for the Camogie Association including a €500,000 annual grant, ticketing, GDPR, vetting, safeguarding, broadcasting, advertising and commercial. “We do all of that together,” he said.

Burns added that they last week outlined the costs of integration to Minister for Sport Patrick O’Donovan and his department officials but he was not prepared to announce them for fear of them being perceived as “prohibitive” to integration. “If I do (reveal the figures), it will come across as the GAA throwing out costs and being prohibitive and not supportive of the process.” 

Burns did reveal they have provided a plan to the Government by which to fund to meet the requirements of integration. He later insisted GAA units should not be charging ladies football and camogie teams for use of their grounds.

The GAA wholeheartedly rejected suggestions of misogyny after McAleese’s claim that some within the organisation are “not entirely happy about the idea of including women in decision-making at the top level of Gaelic sports”.

news.title: ‘He never lost his accent’: How missing Cork native built a happy life as a gay man in England
news.text:
When Patrick O’Sullivan disappeared without a trace in 1992, his family feared what might have happened to him.

The man from Lombardstown, Co Cork was much loved by his late parents and six siblings, but unfortunately it was a very different time in Ireland and he went missing 34 years ago, his family believes, because of his sexuality.

They knew he was gay, but it “wasn’t condoned or even spoken about”, his brother Jerry said.

Patrick ‘Patsy’ O’Sullivan disappeared without a trace just after he visited his family home on Easter Monday in 1992.

He never contacted his family again. 

They received a call from gardaí in August this year, who told them that Patsy went on to have a life “full of joy” in the UK, marrying his partner and retraining as an auxiliary nurse. 

The chef, who was 35 years old at the time, was due to return from his job in Kerry for a christening.

His older brother Jerry said it wasn’t easy for Patsy to grow up gay in the Ireland of the 1970s and 1980s. 

“I was afraid something had happened to him back then (when he went missing) because of his sexuality. Because I remember what happened to me for being a brother of him. I can’t imagine what he went through himself.

“In the 80s and early 1990s that (being gay) wasn’t condoned or even spoken about. It was different times. The church was different. The older people were a very different generation than what they are now.” 

Jerry said Patsy was much loved but circumstances were very difficult. 

“I came up with the old generation. My father would have been very strict. They (his parents) knew (Patsy was gay) but it was never spoken about. My mother didn’t have an issue with it (Patsy being gay) but my father would have. But him being gay was never spoken about.”

[ ‘A closure for us’: Cork family learns brother missing since 1992 died in UK two years agoOpens in new window ]

Patsy went to the UK in 1992 with “nothing” and experienced hard times, before receiving help from a nun called Bridget Anne. 

Life improved for him and in 1994 he met his lifelong partner. Jerry had a heartening hour-long phone call with a niece of Patsy’s partner in the UK on Tuesday.

“It gave me so much solace to what kind of life he had and the enjoyment he had in his life. He had been with his partner since 1994 and he changed his name (to Aldridge) in 1995.” 

He and his partner were married by a priest who knew them very well and Patsy changed his surname in 1995 to take the name of his partner. 

“I can’t think as to what he had to go through as he had to start a life all over again and leave six siblings and his parents behind him. And to never turn back and speak to anyone again. That must have been horrendous for him. 

“I can only imagine what he went through. I can take a lot of comfort from what I am after being told today.”

Jerry was told that Patsy never forgot his Irish roots.

“He never lost his Cork accent and always carried a green, white and gold flag. He always drank from an Irish mug. He drank about 15 cups of tea a day which we do to this present moment. It is a big thing in our family. He was a very proud Irishman and never lost any part of that.”

He went on to train as an auxiliary nurse and Jerry said he was always “on the caring side as a person”. 

His partner died in 2022 and his niece calls Patsy her uncle. 

The O’Sullivan family never gave up looking for Patsy. Jerry and his brother Eugene made an appeal for information as recently as two years ago on RTÉ’s Crimecall. 

Heartbreakingly, it has emerged that Patsy was living just over an hour away from a brother who died in the UK last year. 

“I used to go over to my brother in the UK eight or ten times a year. I was very close to my eldest brother. And Patsy was only an hour up the road. That is a killer.”

Patsy died of sepsis two years ago and his ashes were spread alongside the ashes of his late partner in a place that meant a lot to them in London. 

Jerry plans to put a memory box together for Patsy. He also intends to put his name on a headstone in order to give him the closure that he deserves in his native country. 

The case was investigated by gardaí when Patsy went missing. Jerry says that in recent years Garda PJ Roche and his team left no stone unturned in order to find out what happened to him. 

“Since 2015 checks were done with DNA, Interpol, Canada, Australia, America, New Zealand, England, Scotland and Wales. Everything came back a blank even down to the John Does who were dead and buried and had no name. It was looking bleak.”

He was astonished when he found out what had happened to him. He plans to travel there next month to speak to people who knew him. 

“I am going to meet as many people and get as many stories as I can. I believe Patsy started looking very like our brother Eugene (as he got older).”

He cherishes his memories of his wonderful brother and adds he hopes that people who go missing realise that they can always go home. 

[ Behind the mystery that first set off fears of Iranian threats at a UK military baseOpens in new window ]
news.summary: Patsy O’Sullivan disappeared without trace on Easter Monday from Lombardstown, Co Cork in 1992
news.author: Olivia Kelleher

news.title: Leinster hurling revolution promises more jeopardy and a new route to the top
news.text: The proposed new format for the Leinster Senior Hurling Championship has something for everyone. After years of stagnation, the radical shake-up promises greater jeopardy for the province’s big guns while giving emerging counties a clearer route towards the top table. And former GAA president Nickey Brennan , who chaired the reform committee, believes they have finally found the balance between protecting the leading counties and giving the likes of Kildare, Antrim, Carlow, Laois and Westmeath a genuine pathway forward. The biggest change is that the Leinster Championship will effectively be split into two groups from 2028. The teams who finish first to fourth in next year’s championship will be placed in Group A, while the sides finishing fifth and sixth will be joined by the 2027 Joe McDonagh Cup finalists in Group B. But being in Group B will not mean the end of Leinster ambitions. Far from it. Five new knockout games will be introduced, creating a much greater element of jeopardy and giving the second-tier counties a chance to bridge the gap to the Liam McCarthy Cup. At present, Leinster has 31 games but only one knockout fixture — the final. Under the new structure there will be 30 games, but six of them will be knockout matches. The teams finishing third and fourth in Group A will enter the quarter-finals against the teams finishing first and second in Group B. The four quarter-finalists will then be involved in an open draw to determine the semi-final pairings. The two teams who finish first and second in Group A will enter at the semi-final stage, where they will face the quarter-final winners. The Leinster final will then be played alongside a third-place play-off between the beaten semi-finalists, with the winner of that game claiming the third Leinster place in the All-Ireland quarter-finals. And Brennan believes the new format will end the dreaded “yo-yo” effect which has seen counties bounce between the Joe McDonagh Cup and the Liam McCarthy Championship. “The feedback we got from all the teams in Leinster was that this yo-yoing effect is not helping us at all,” said Brennan. “We need to get some sort of certainty. “By coming up with this formula, it does give teams certainty. If you're in Group B, it's very much up to yourself now to work your way up through Group B. “At a minimum, finish sixth in Group B, which means you're in the Leinster knockout quarter-final and you're up against perhaps big hitters. “I can tell you from engaging with them that the likes of Antrim are bursting to get into Group B. “They now see a target for how they get to the final of the Joe McDonagh Cup in 2027 and get into Group B the following year. So it's very much within their own control.” The new system will also crank up the pressure on the established counties. The top four will still have the advantage of avoiding the quarter-finals if they finish first or second in Group A — but there will be no margin for error for those who finish third or fourth. “The jeopardy level has changed,” said Brennan. “The two Group A teams who don't get to a semi-final are gone if they lose their quarter-final. That's them gone — their season is over. “So the composition of the four teams in Group A could change from one year to the next. “And the same at Group B, depending on who's there. If you're not in A, you'll end up in B. “So there's a fair lot of possibilities here with this. But the ball is very much in every county's court. “You'd want to be getting first or second in Group A and avoiding the quarter-finals. And then your concerns are over.” There is also a workload benefit for the teams who perform best in the group stage. Brennan says there will be breaks built into the schedule, meaning teams finishing in the top two in Group A could have three weekends without a competitive fixture during the campaign. “Obviously, if you get first or second, you're going to avoid the quarter-finals. That's another break of a week. And there'll be a break before the final. “The final and the third-place play-off will be played on the one weekend. “So if you come first or second in the eight-week competition, you have three weekends blank. So the better you perform, the better you're going to give your players an opportunity to have breaks here.” But the biggest winners could be the Tier 2 counties who have been caught in the Leinster-Joe McDonagh merry-go-round. Kildare’s struggles this year highlighted the gap between the two levels, despite their ability to compete with the province’s strongest sides for long periods. Under the new system, there is now a defined route forward. “The Tier 2 counties are excited about this because it now gives them some certainty about a pathway forward,” said Brennan. “In the past, it was all about, if we come sixth, we're gone anyway. You know, now you can come sixth. “Whoever comes sixth next year in Leinster is actually going to be in Group B as the second team in Group B. And at least they're starting off 2028 in that position. “Now, what they have to then try and do is win their matches to stay first or second in order to contest the quarter-finals of the Leinster Championship. “So there's lots of possibilities here.” Click here to sign up to our sport newsletter, bringing you the top stories and biggest headlines from Ireland and beyond
news.summary: Radical new format will give Tier 2 counties a clearer pathway while putting the province’s big guns under pressure
news.author: Garry Doyle

news.title: Former Derry hurler Brendan ‘Benny’ Ward dies aged 52
news.text: Former Derry hurler Brendan ‘Benny’ Ward has died at the age of 52. Ward was a key member of the Derry side that won back-to-back Ulster titles in 2000 and 2001. He also played in the Oak Leaf county’s famous near-miss against Offaly in the 2000 All-Ireland Championship, when Derry came agonisingly close to pulling off a major upset. Paying tribute, Derry GAA said: “Benny was a kind and gentle soul. He loved hurling. He loved his community. And he gave much to both. “Derry GAA is deeply saddened by the death of Brendan ‘Benny’ Ward.” Click here to sign up to our sport newsletter, bringing you the top stories and biggest headlines from Ireland and beyond
news.summary: Ward excelled during Derry hurling's golden spell in 2000 and 2001.

news.title: Next Monday set as date for major meeting about malting
news.text:
A major meeting of malting barley growers will take place next Monday, (October 12) to discuss urgent issues affecting the sector.

The Irish Farmers' Association (IFA) will host the meeting at the Dolmen Hotel, Carlow, and Boortmalt representatives have also been invited to attend.

“We have already asked Boortmalt to waive the €10/t drying charge on 2026 crops," Murphy told Agriland.

“But, as yet, we have not received a reply from the company on this matter.

“It’s important that Boortmalt representatives attend the Carlow event.”

Malting meeting

The IFA had been looking for a formal meeting with Boortmalt, but this was declined until late last week when Boortmalt said they would only meet on condition that those representing IFA sign a legal non-disclosure agreement (NDA).

"This would mean that we could not report back to our members on the meeting. This is not acceptable," Murphy continued.

“We feel it is absolutely imperative that Boortmalt meets to discuss the lack of a malting premium and the so-called €10/t parity charge in place for Harvest 2026.

“We would encourage all malting barley growers to be in Carlow on Monday night.”

The meeting will get underway at the Dolmen Hotel, Carlow at 8:00p.m next Monday.

news.title: Horse suffers fatal injury after head-on collision with outrider after making winning debut
news.text: A racehorse has died following a devastating head-on collision with an outrider just moments after securing victory on her debut. Two year old Stringin Me On was competing for the first time in a maiden special weight at Assiniboia Downs in Winnipeg, Canada on Monday night. Breaking sharply from the gates, she dominated throughout under jockey Rachaad Knights, surging clear of her three opponents in the home straight to triumph by five lengths. Just four of the five starters finished the five-and-a-half-furlong contest after Onemoresteptoheaven struck the rail early on and unseated its rider. Tragedy struck after Knights had crossed the line and was returning Stringin Me On towards the winners' circle. While trotting back, they were unable to avoid an outrider who had caught Onemoresteptoheaven and collided directly with Stringin Me On, reports the Mirror . Both riders were thrown into the air while the horses crashed to the ground. Simultaneously, stewards launched an inquiry into the race following multiple objections from jockeys regarding interference. Veterinary staff rushed to treat the fallen horses but sadly were unable to save Stringin Me On. A statement from the racecourse confirmed: "A very unfortunate situation occurred at ASD on Monday night when a loose horse was gathered by the outrider and his horse and then they collided with another horse after the race had concluded. "We can advise that the initial loose horse and the horse belonging to the outrider were unharmed, however, the single horse returning after the race suffered injuries and did not survive. "The outrider and jockey Rachaad Knights were both okay and uninjured and the jockey rode during Tuesday's live races." In a further setback for Stringin Me On's owners, Dark Cloud Racing, and trainer Judy Hunter, the unfortunate filly was later stripped of her placing after stewards accepted an objection regarding early interference from the rider of Ringit, who had finished in last position. news.summary: Stringin Me On won on her debut by five lengths at Assiniboia Downs in Winnipeg, Canada, but suffered a fatal injury after a post-race collision with an outrider on Monday night

news.title: Murphy hat-trick powers Midleton CBS to Dean Ryan win
news.text:
While a 14-point margin at the end was rough justice on the hosts at the Mon Field, there was no arguing that the visitors were deserving of victory, earning the right to garnish the scoreline with late goals.

In windy and intermittently wet conditions, it was an attritional battle. In Murphy and Conor Ronayne, Midleton displayed more of a cutting edge and looked likelier winners at half-time, when they led by 0-8 to 0-5 having played into the worst of the elements.

While Gaelcholáiste Mhuire’s main attacking threat, Séamus Ó Donnabháin, pointed within seconds of the restart, it was as close as they would come for the remainder – Midleton produced a strong riposte with points from Ronayne and Murphy (two).

Aided by the strength of a half-back line where Roan Kelleher impressed, Midleton could have moved further clear in the third quarter but their shooting let them down. At the other end, they had reason to be thankful to goalkeeper Will Stokes – a county minor winner with Midleton on Monday night – for a fine save to deny Ryan Ó Corráin at a time when a goal would brought ‘the AG’ to within a point.

Midleton were not without their own goal chances though: Tomás Ó Sé was unlucky to send a low shot wide after a good run on 51 but they didn’t have too long to wait as Murphy pounced on the break when an Eoghan O’Donovan clearance broke and slotted home for a 1-11 to 0-7 advantage.

The attacker almost added another immediately after that, firing across the face of the goal, but after Gaelcholáiste Mhuire centre-back Mixie Gale landed a big free for what would be their last score, Midleton went into overdrive.

A great catch from sub Ben Aherne was the catalyse for an Ó Sé point before Murphy got his second goal following a counter-attack.

Sub Bill Leahy made it 2-13 to 0-8 and deep injury time Murphy got his hat-trick goal.

Goal chances had been rare in the first half, where Midleton moved into an early 0-4 to 0-1 lead as they moved the ball well only for two Cillian Mac Eocháin frees and an Ó Donnabháin point to bring the home side level.

Murphy, set up by James Doyle, had Midleton back in front before a free from goalkeeper Stokes had them 0-6 to 0-4 in front. They would lead thereafter.

news.title: Full list of social welfare payments set for €520 increase from January
news.text: Budget 2027 was recently announced as the government revealed a slate of measures set to come into effect. An increase to core social welfare rates have become a staple of budget measures, and this year was no different. Over a million people will see their payments increase from January by €10 a week, or €520 a year. They have confirmed the full list of payments in line for the increase. The full list of payments increased were: State Pension (Contributory) State Pension (Non-Contributory) Bereaved Partner's (Contributory) Pension Bereaved Partner's (Non-Contributory) Pension Jobseeker's Benefit Jobseeker's Allowance One-Parent Family Payment Maternity Benefit Adoptive Benefit Paternity Benefit Parent’s Benefit Health and Safety Benefit Farm Assist Deserted Wife's Benefit Deserted Wife's Allowance Supplementary Welfare Allowance Illness Benefit Invalidity Pension Disability Allowance Blind Pension Injury Benefit Disablement Benefit Death Benefit Scheme Carer's Benefit Carer's Allowance Guardian’s payment As well as the €10 core increase, the Child Support Payment weekly rate will increase by: €6, from €58 to €64, for children under 12 €6, from €78 to €84, for children aged 12 and over Fuel Allowance will increase by €5 from €38 to €43 per week. The Living Alone Increase will increase by €3 from €22 to €25 per week. The Living on a Specified Island Allowance will increase by €5 from €20 to €25 per week. A cost of disability payment of €500 will be paid to people getting a long-term disability payment. The lump sum will be paid in 2027. It is for people on long-term disability payments and will benefit 240 thousand people. A Christmas bonus of 100% will also be paid to people getting a qualifying social welfare payment the week starting 7 December 2026. Get the full rundown on Tuesday's budget announcement here . news.summary: Budget 2027 was announced on Tuesday and with it the Department of Social Protection announced a rate increase to core social welfare payments - here's all the details

news.title: Roy Keane tears into 'sloppy' England and Arsenal star
news.text: Roy Keane believes Eberechi Eze displays too many careless moments in his performances for Arsenal and England. The former Manchester United skipper has called on him to rise to the competitive demands at both club and international level. Eze, 28, featured in England's starting XI for their Nations League fixture against Czechia and completed the entire 90 minutes of their 3-0 victory. This marks only the second occasion he has avoided being either brought on or taken off across his 25 international appearances. Both instances occurred under Thomas Tuchel, the previous being in the friendly defeat to Senegal last June. Additionally, all bar one of his six starts have taken place since the ex-Chelsea manager assumed control 18 months ago. Prior to Tuesday's match at Wembley Stadium, the player's brief appearance after coming on for Anthony Gordon in the 70th minute of their 7-0 thrashing of Croatia attracted disapproval. Keane told ITV: "I was disappointed with him the other night when he came on. "Obviously, England are attacking and doing really well, so when you get opportunities, you've got to take them. I thought he was really sloppy with some of his play, so it's a big opportunity for him tonight.", reports the Mirror . Keane went on to stress the significance of the fixture for Eze: "It's a big test for him tonight. We know how good he is at coming and getting the ball. "But we didn't see that running power off the ball [against Croatia]. I'm not sure whether he really wants to do it or is unaware he's not doing it, but I think it's a big night for him." 'When you look at the attacking players and the challenges, and I'm including Arsenal, sometimes in his play he can just be a bit sloppy. He needs to bring his A-game. Discussing mentality more broadly, before returning his attention to Eze, the former footballer said: "I just worry sometimes players are going: 'Oh, it's not my time, or he's better than me'.... "Embrace that challenge that the other players have brought to the England squad and at Arsenal. He seems just to shy away from it, embrace that and bring your A-game. "As I said, I've watched him far too many times, and there are just too many sloppy moments. Keane's ITV colleague Ian Wright defended the player, stating: "He's got a playing style where if you're sloppy and you're playing with that languid kind of style, then it can look worse than it is.. "I'm not saying he should change his style. But he just needs to tighten everything up a bit because he's an amazing player." news.title: Southampton boss Tonda Eckert given suspended six-week ban and fine over Spygate
news.text:
Eckert accepted full responsibility and was charged by the FA with three breaches of Rule E3.1 in relation to “misconduct”, which hung over Southampton and their manager heading into the new campaign.

The German coach attended an FA hearing at the start of the international break and is able to continue his role against rivals Portsmouth this Sunday and beyond.

A statement from the governing body read: “Tonda Eckert subsequently admitted the charges, and an independent Regulatory Commission imposed a six-week suspension from all football and football related activity, which is suspended until the end of the 2027/28 season, a £28,000 fine and a reprimand following a hearing.

“The suspended sanction will come into effect in the event he is found to have committed a breach of Rules or Regulations by requesting, authorising, taking, or using information from any observation of the training of another club, in whatever guise that observation may take.” The punishment is likely to draw strong opinions from across the game, with Southampton saying in a statement “this now brings a conclusion to a regrettable period of our history”.

The club, who sit 13th in the Championship, say “measures have been put in place to ensure that such errors in judgement never happen again at our club” and they are “excited to move forward together towards a bright future”.

Southampton owner Dragan Solak said: “I’m pleased that the independent panel has come to a decision and that we have an outcome.

“We have already suffered enough, and we appreciate the panel’s recognition of that.

“We are confident the manager has learned from this matter, and a suspended sentence allows him to continue in his role.

“I firmly believe that Tonda is one of Europe’s most exciting young coaches, and with this distraction removed, I am confident he can lead the team to a successful season. I’d like to thank our fans for standing by us and showing the team so much support during a time when we have needed them more than ever.

“The FA process has been a positive experience. Tonda has been given the opportunity to be open and honest with the panel, and the panel has been able to see that he is simply a good person who made poor decisions.

“The same cannot be said for the EFL process, and the way they have subsequently treated us is not something we will forget.

“However, now is the time to look forward to what I believe will be a great future for our club.” The English Football League declined to comment.
news.summary: Saints were kicked out of the Championship play-off final and docked four points this term having admitted three breaches of EFL regulations after being caught snooping on semi-final opponents Middlesbrough and two other teams.

news.title: Simon Harris responds to scathing comments by RTÉ's Oliver Callan who labelled him a 'college dropout'
news.text: Simon Harris has responded to scathing comments made by RTÉ’s Oliver Callan, who said the Tánaiste is a "college drop out" who is as "unpopular as Donald Trump". The satirist is known for impersonating politicians and taking them down a peg, and often gets away with it. However, people were quick to brand a recent column the RTÉ broadcaster wrote for the Irish Independent as classist. The piece was widely shared on social media with the eye-catching headline: "That’s right, our €600bn economy is in the grip of a college dropout who likes TikTok and Coldplay." In the piece written before the budget, Mr Callan wrote: "Next week, a college dropout will deliver the budget for our €600bn economy. "Don’t be too alarmed – Simon Harris isn’t actually making all the key decisions. There are serious people for that sort of thing." Mr Callan was questioning the Tánaiste’s credentials, after he took over the finance portfolio last November following his colleague Paschal Donohoe’s departure. But even sharp-tongued Ivan Yates said the broadcaster was talking "total shite" in the column, brandishing it as "absolute snobbery" and "nonsense". Speaking on the State of Affairs podcast, the former Fine Gael minister said: "You can say Simon Harris lacks substance, he tries to be all things to all people. There’s a million things, but to attack being a dropout from college as being unsuitable to be minister for finance….it’s absolute snobbery." Mr Yates himself, a broadcaster and businessman, didn’t complete his Leaving Cert, instead attending agricultural college and running the family farm at 16 years old when his father was diagnosed with cancer. The Tánaiste dropped out of a journalism degree at the DIT to focus on autism activism and politics. At 22 he gained a seat in Wicklow County Council, and became a TD in the Dáil two years later. Mr Callan also studied journalism, completing his degree from DCU in the early 2000s before working in various newsrooms and entering the comedy scene. On Tuesday, Mr Harris delivered his first budget as finance minister, a package the opposition have criticised for giving money to people who already have it. Just four days before this his wife Caoimhe gave birth to a baby girl, the couple's third child. With a budget and baby all in one week, the Tánaiste wasn’t too keen on lashing back at his RTÉ critic. Asked what his thoughts were on the column and the "college dropout" comment, the Finance Minister told us: "I haven't really thought about it. I've had a pretty busy week. But, yeah, Oliver… Oliver is…. we live in a free country." Subscribe to our newsletter for the latest news from the Irish Mirror direct to your inbox: Sign up here.

news.title: Woman’s High Court case against adult websites adjourned over $120m US settlement
news.text:
A High Court case in which a woman claims recordings of her being sexually abused as child appeared on adult websites associated with Pornhub has been adjourned for six months after a judge was told that approval is awaited of a $120 million (€107 million) settlement of an associated class action in the United States.

The woman, who lives in the US and has been given the name “Jane Doe” to protect her identity, claims she was drugged and raped by a man when she was a minor.

She claims her abuser recorded what happened and posted the images online.

It is alleged that videos of her abuse were published and distributed on adult video-sharing websites owned by the group of companies that own, control and manage internet pornography websites including Pornhub.

As a result, a class action on behalf of the woman and others has been brought in the US courts against various parties within the MindGeek (now renamed AYLO) group of companies. MindGeek, before its name change, is Pornhub’s parent. 

The woman’s allegations of wrongdoing by the group have been denied.

In a damages claim before the US courts, the woman alleges she has been victimised and has been exploited by the defendants for profit.

Due to the international structure of the defendant group, the woman sought to bring parallel proceedings before the Irish courts. It is also alleged that the Irish entities have substantial assets.

The defendants in the Irish action include the limited companies AYLO Billing, Mirmay, Nutaku Publishing, Appatomic and Liquidum, which all have a registered address at The Black Church, St Mary’s Place, Dublin. 

Other defendants in her proceedings also include MG Freesites Ltd, MG Freesites II Ltd, AYLO Premium Ltd, MG Social Ltd, MindGeek USA Incorporated and MindGeek SARL, which is registered in Luxembourg.

In her Irish proceeding the woman seeks orders including aggravated and exemplary damages for what she claims is the defendants breach of duty and for breaches of GDPR, conspiracy and her right to privacy.

She also wants an order directing the defendants to identify and remove images of child sexual abuse from the websites and the identities of users who have uploaded the images.

The woman also wants an order directing the defendants to preserve all assets and cash reserves in Ireland below an amount of $630 million pending the outcome of the actions in Ireland and the US.

In the US, the defendants recently agreed to settle a class action, on behalf of the woman and others depicted in the material, and pay $120 million. 

MindGeek also agreed to injunctive relief which will see it make substantial changes to its sites in order to protect children. The settlement is subject to court approval in the US.

The Irish case was back before the High Court on Wednesday when barrister Robert O’Reilly, for the woman, sought an adjournment to allow for the approval of a $120 million settlement of the US proceedings in Alabama. 

Judge Brian Cregan adjourned the case to March.
news.summary: ‘Jane Doe’ says recordings of her being abused as a minor were published on video-sharing sites

news.title: RTÉ rejects minister’s claim reforms have been slow as €20m funding cut confirmed
news.text:
His comments came as the Government confirmed that RTÉ will receive €240m in 2027, €20m less than the broadcaster had been anticipating under its multi-annual funding agreement.

Mr O’Donovan said the €11m increase in funding for RTÉ accounted for a large part of his department’s additional funding for 2027. If RTÉ were given its full €260m allocation, he said, this would represent nearly 70% of his department’s budget uplift.

RTÉ is currently in the middle of a €725m three-year multi-annual agreement with the Government, but sources said there had been concerns about the pace of contingent reforms, a charge RTÉ has rejected.

Mr Bakhurst said the reduced funding would mean RTÉ “has important decisions to make”, given commitments already made to audiences, the independent sector, other stakeholders and staff.

“The Government's decision to reduce this public funding agreement by €20m at this late stage, when we have already made important commitments to our audiences, to the independent sector, to other important stakeholders and to RTÉ staff, is one we had not anticipated and will inevitably impact on our ability to deliver our five-year strategy.” 

RTÉ seeks meeting with minister 

Mr Bakhurst said RTÉ chair Terence O’Rourke was seeking a meeting with the minister regarding the multi-annual commitment made in 2024, “particularly given that RTÉ has committed to numerous agreements with its stakeholders based on this written and extensively publicised agreement”.

“In fact, the Taoiseach and the Tánaiste said at the time, that predictable multi-annual funding is key to RTÉ being able to deliver a strategy.” 

Mr Bakhurst said the clarity provided by the multi-annual funding agreement had enabled RTÉ to plan ahead, deliver trusted and independent news and analysis, produce more public service programmes and content, including original Irish drama and live sport, and invest in podcasts, apps and the RTÉ Player.

He also said the agreement had enabled RTÉ to implement a digital commercial strategy, stabilise its finances and progress its plans.
news.summary: Kevin Bakhurst said RTÉ had made commitments based on its multi-annual agreement and warned the funding reduction would affect its strategy

news.title: Morta Maricarmen Abascal, simbolo della lotta per il diritto alla casa in Spagna
news.text:
E’ morta Maricarmen Abascal, la signora spagnola di 87 anni divenuta il simbolo delle proteste per il diritto alla casa in Spagna. La donna, all'anagrafe Maria del Carmen Abascal, è deceduta all’ospedale "Gregorio Maranon" di Madrid, dov'era ricoverata dallo scorso 23 settembre, dopo lo sfratto coatto avvenuto in diretta televisiva su una barella dalla sua abitazione nel quartiere del Retiro, nella quale aveva vissuto per 70 anni.
La notizia della morte dell’anziana, che per 7 anni aveva affrontato una battaglia giudiziaria contro lo sfratto, è stata diffusa dal Sindicato de Inquilinas, che l’aveva affiancata nella lotta. "Ci duole comunicare che nella giornata odierna è morta Maricarmen", ha informato in un messaggio sui social. "Lo scorso 23 settembre, come tutti sapete, si era realizzato il suo sgombero e da allora era rimasta in ospedale. Sebbene si è poi stato raggiunto uno storico accordo che le avrebbe permesso di tornare nella sua abitazione, questa soluzione è arrivata troppo tardi", segnala il sindacato, che definisce lo sfratto dell’anziana "una situazione di assolutamente evitabile, dopo un processo di tortura".
La vicenda dell’anziana signora diventata icona dei movimenti di lotta per il diritto alla casa aveva avuto una svolta relativamente veloce: la sera di lunedì 28 settembre, infatti, era stato reso noto un accordo tra la società Urbagestión, proprietaria dell’abitazione in cui la donna aveva risieduto per 70 anni, e la sua famiglia, tramite legale, per permetterle di tornare a vivere nello stesso alloggio, pagando un affitto sostenibile. Il giorno dopo, la stessa Maricarmen, che aveva anche un grado di disabilità riconosciuta del 50%, aveva accettato le nuove condizioni. Il suo ritorno a casa, dunque, sarebbe stato possibile non appena fosse stata dimessa dall’ospedale in cui è rimasta ricoverata dal giorno dello sfratto. Ma dall'ospedale Maricarmen non ha fatto in tempo a uscire.
"Gli eventi scatenati dall’ingiustizia dello sfratto" di Maricarmen "rappresentano un prima e un dopo nella storia della Spagna", ha rimarcato il Sindicato de Inquilinas. "Il dibattito sulla casa è al centro dell’attenzione, ma il prezzo pagato per arrivare fin qui è stato troppo alto", prosegue la nota. "Ora ci rimane l’esempio di lotta e l’eredità che Maricarmen ci ha lasciato. E, soprattutto, faremo ciò che lei ci ha sempre chiesto: 'lottate, continuate a lottare per ciò che è vostro'. La tua famiglia, la tua avvocatessa e il tuo sindacato continueremo a difendere il diritto alla casa e a lottare contro gli speculatori, con la forza e il coraggio che ci hai insegnato. Continueremo a lottare per te, per tutte, come hai sempre voluto", ha assicurato il sindacato.

news.title: La condannata a morte Christa Pike al risveglio: "Dove sono e chi sei?"
news.text: "Dove sono e chi sei?": queste sono state le prime parole di Christa Pike dopo aver ripreso coscienza in ospedale martedì sera, quasi una settimana dopo l'esecuzione fallita. La sopravvissuta a una doppia iniezione letale in Tennessee è ora in grado di parlare, hanno detto i suoi avvocati, ma è ancora confusa, arrabbiata e non le ancora chiaro cosa le sia successo quel 30 settembre, quando il suo caso è salito alla ribalta mondiale., Pike, hanno detto i legali in una conferenza stampa convocata dopo l'udienza in cui un giudice di Nashville ha ordinato al dipartimento delle prigioni di preservare tutte le prove legate al flop del boia, ha contratto una polmonite e ha un trombo in un braccio. Non può ancora mangiare perché non riesce a inghiottire.

news.title: Anna Lou Castoldi, l'amico le ruba il telefono e pubblica un suo video intimo: la figlia di Asia Argento e Morgan vittima di furto e revenge porn
news.text: Prima la lite, poi il furto del telefono e la pubblicazione di un video privato sui porifli social. È quanto accaduto a Anna Lou Castoldi, figlia di Asia Argento e Morgan. I fatti si sarebbero verificati tra Napoli e Licola, località a nord del capoluogo campano. La dinamica Il furto sarebbe avvenuto, secondo quanto finora ricostruito, in una struttura ricettiva della zona di Licola, nell'hinterland a nord di Napoli. L'uomo si è poi allontanato per recarsi in piazza Garibaldi dove è stato trovato in stato confusionale. Durante lo spostamento a Napoli avrebbe pubblicato il video, probabilmente dopo avere litigato con la 25enne. La denuncia A lanciare l'allarme è stata proprio Asia Argento che dopo essersi accorta delle immagini su Instagram ha tentato inutilmente di contattare la figlia. A questo punto si è rivolta alla polizia, che è riuscita a geolocalizzare il telefono insieme con la borsa nelle mani dell'amico. Gli agenti hanno prima accompagnato l'uomo in ospedale - trovato in stato confusionale - per affidarlo alle cure dei sanitari e poi lo hanno denunciato per revenge porn, furto e accesso abusivo a sistema informatico. Sul caso, la Procura di Napoli ha aperto un'inchiesta affidata alla sezione fasce deboli.

news.title: Il gasolio sale ancora, accise mobili dopo i tetti delle compagnie: cosa succede
news.text: Finito lo sconto fiscale, il gasolio continua a salire: oggi è arrivato a 2,261 euro. Il governo non esclude di intervenire di nuovo con le accise mobili, che hanno messo in cassa 170 milioni, e sta valutando se usarli solo alla fine dei price cap delle compagnie. In Ue si accende invece il dibattito sulla tassazione degli extraprofitti delle società energetiche. L'Eni invece va in controtendenza e abbassa di 4 centesimi il prezzo del suo diesel alla pompa. Il ministero delle Imprese registra che oggi è diminuito il costo della benzina, ed è salito quello del gasolio. Sulle strade ordinarie, in modalità 'self service' la benzina costa 2,040 euro al litro (2,243 martedì), il gasolio 2,261 (2,244 euro il prezzo di martedì). Il gasolio sale ancora, accise mobili dopo i tetti delle compagnie Ieri è finito lo sconto fiscale di 6,1 centesimi sul diesel messo dal governo, e i quattro maggiori gruppi petroliferi che operano in Italia (Eni, Ip, Q8 e Tamoil) hanno alzato in modo equivalente il loro price cap. Quello di Eni adesso è di 2,25 euro per il gasolio (era 2,19) e di 1,99 euro per la benzina (invariato). Ad alzare la media del diesel sono i piccoli operatori, le «pompe bianche», che non hanno le dimensioni per fare sconti: il loro prezzo medio è di 2,28 euro al litro. Oggi però Eni ha deciso di abbassare il costo del suo gasolio di 4 centesimi, portandolo a 2,21 euro al litro. Secondo il sito di energia Staffetta Quotidiana, si tratta di una mossa commerciale, a seguito di un brusco calo delle quotazioni internazionali dei prodotti raffinati. La posizione di Meloni La premier Giorgia Meloni a metà settembre si era impegnata a proseguire gli sconti fiscali dal 6 ottobre, con il meccanismo delle accise mobili, cioè il taglio delle accise usando l'extragettito dell'Iva sul petrolio del mese precedente. Ma dopo che i grandi gruppi hanno deciso di mettere il price cap sui carburanti, ha preferito terminare il calmiere pubblico, che andava avanti da marzo, ed è costato alle casse dello stato 4,7 miliardi. E' pronta però a far riscattare il meccanismo. «Noi siamo sempre pronti a intervenire di nuovo, particolarmente con il meccanismo delle accise mobili - ha detto la premier -. Al mese di settembre abbiamo circa 170 milioni che possono essere spesi per questo obiettivo. Ci stiamo interrogando se sia più efficace spenderli in questo momento, in cui comunque ci sono misure di contenimento, o tenerle come provvista quando dovessero terminare quelle misure. Dipende anche dalla tenuta del cap. Vediamo cosa accade nelle prossime ore». Le compagnie petrolifere «Eni condivide le necessità espresse dal Presidente del Consiglio», ha risposto il gruppo a stretto giro, «e sta applicando, e applicherà, una politica commerciale responsabile», per «mantenere i prezzi a un livello sostenibile». Il price cap «avrà la funzione di contenere eventuali livelli di picco». Il problema non è solo italiano, tanto che per evitare rialzi eccessivi, gli Stati membri dell'Agenzia internazionale dell'Energia (Iea) hanno annunciato da Parigi di essere «pronti a rilasciare ulteriori riserve strategiche (di carburante, n.d.r.) se necessario». La presidenza di turno irlandese della Ue intanto ha rimesso sul tavolo l'ipotesi di una tassazione degli extraprofitti delle società energetiche. Parlando al Parlamento europeo di Strasburgo, il ministro Thomas Byrne ha detto che, visti «i prezzi dei combustibili fossili che crescono a non finire e il costo della vita che è aumentato in modo significativo, è necessario mitigare le conseguenze negative per cittadini e bisogna tassare le società energetiche». Se ne parlerà venerdì all'Ecofin in Lussemburgo. Il tema energia preoccupa ovviamente le imprese e scalda il confronto politico. Assoaeroporti guarda con preoccupazione ai prezzi del jet fuel: non ci sono problemi di quantità - evidenzia - ma il carburante pesa per il 31% sui costi dei voli e potrebbe portare a rincari e annullamenti. L'allarme arriva anche da Confindustria Ceramiche che sottolinea come i costi sull'energia «metta in ginocchio» il settore. «Cosa sta facendo il governo Meloni per mettere fine alle crisi geopolitiche, alle guerre che stanno avendo ripercussioni profonde sulle tasche degli italiani? La risposta è niente -, ha attaccato la leader dem Elly Schlein -. Noi abbiamo insistito per tassare gli extraprofitti delle società energetiche, anziché rimettersi alla loro clemenza e alla loro buona volontà, e per riattivare il meccanismo delle accise mobili».
news.summary: Finito lo sconto fiscale, il gasolio continua a salire: oggi è arrivato a 2,261 euro. Il governo non esclude di intervenire di nuovo con le accise mobili, che hanno messo in cassa 170...

news.title: Zelensky, 'oggi 25 vittime in Ucraina, 5 i bimbi uccisi'
news.text: ROMA, 07 OTT - "Oggi, per tutta la giornata, sono continuati i lavori di rimozione delle macerie dopo l'attacco del missile russo a Pryluky. Si trattava di un missile Kh-101, che ha colpito direttamente un edificio. Purtroppo, 19 persone sono morte, tra cui cinque bambini piccoli. In totale, il numero di vittime a seguito di questo massiccio attacco all'Ucraina è di 25 persone. Cento persone sono rimaste ferite". E' il bilancio serale del presidente ucraino Volodymyr Zelensky sui social. "È fondamentale che i leader non rimangano in silenzio di fronte a ciò che è accaduto perché la Russia intende continuare verso l'escalation, verso l'uccisione". (ANSA).

news.title: Incendio a Giulianova, fiamme fermate prima delle case
news.text: GIULIANOVA, 07 OTT - Un vasto incendio ha minacciato nel pomeriggio il centro abitato di Giulianova paese, in provincia di Teramo. Le fiamme hanno mandato in fumo circa quattro ettari di macchia mediterranea, sviluppandosi pericolosamente a ridosso delle aree residenziali. L'emergenza ha richiesto un massiccio dispiegamento di forze. Sul posto sono intervenute le squadre dei Vigili del Fuoco del Comando provinciale di Teramo e dei distaccamenti di Roseto degli Abruzzi e Nereto. L'intenso lavoro da terra ha permesso di circoscrivere progressivamente il fronte del rogo, sbarrando la strada al fuoco prima che potesse raggiungere le case. Fondamentale per il controllo dell'incendio è stato il supporto aereo: un elicottero del Reparto Volo dei Vigili del Fuoco di Pescara ha sorvolato la zona effettuando numerosi sganci d'acqua sui punti più critici. Una volta arginata l'avanzata delle fiamme, le squadre hanno proceduto alle operazioni di bonifica per scongiurare la ripartenza di focolai nascosti. All'intervento hanno collaborato attivamente anche i volontari dell'Antincendio Boschivo (AIB) delle associazioni Gran Sasso d'Italia (sezione di Mosciano Sant'Angelo), ANA di Atri, Nova di Città Sant'Angelo e il Gruppo di Protezione Civile locale di Giulianova. (ANSA).
news.author: Ansa

news.title: Con Aurora & Nick Spinatelli la canzone italiana si mette a ballare
news.text: ROMA, 07 OTT - Da Guarda che luna ad Ancora tu, da Per un'ora d'amore a Comprami. Le canzoni che hanno attraversato generazioni possono cambiare veste senza perdere la propria identità. È da questo incontro tra repertorio italiano e ritmo dance che nasce "Italianissima", l'album d'esordio di Aurora & Nick Spinatelli. Nove tracce, otto reinterpretazioni e un brano originale raccontano decenni, autori e immaginari differenti: dal Quartetto Cetra di "Un bacio a mezzanotte" a Fred Buscaglione, presente con "Guarda che luna" e "Love in Portofino", fino a Lucio Battisti, Matia Bazar, Gianna Nannini e Viola Valentino. Il singolo scelto per le radio è "Un bacio a mezzanotte", brano del 1952 nato per la rivista Gran Baraonda e reso popolare dal Quartetto Cetra. "È una canzone che tutti in Italia conoscono, spesso senza nemmeno sapere quando l'hanno ascoltata per la prima volta. La nostra versione è nata sul palco, durante i nostri set nei club. Abbiamo voluto creare un contrasto netto tra una scrittura degli anni Cinquanta e una cassa dritta contemporanea. È esattamente il dialogo tra passato e presente che volevamo costruire con tutto l'album", racconta il duo. La dimensione live è centrale nella storia di "Italianissima" dato che Aurora e Nick si esibiscono con continuità tra club e location. Il titolo dell'album coincide con quello dell'unico brano inedito, "Italianissima", scritto da Aurora & Nick Spinatelli. Il pezzo racconta un mondo fatto di cinema, moda, estati italiane, cultura popolare e rappresenta il lato più personale del duo, tra atmosfere Italo-disco e malinconie ricercate, in cui tutto arriva senza sembrare mai forzato: canzoni prese in prestito per immaginare dove potranno ancora andare. (ANSA).
news.author: Ansa

news.title: Il mistero dei 4 georgiani fermati con passaporti falsi verso Tel Aviv
news.text: Quattro georgiani, un uomo e una donna sulla quarantina, un'altra donna, un minorenne. Sarebbero arrivati insieme a Bologna da Istanbul il 4 ottobre, poi il giorno dopo si sono divisi: i primi due hanno tentato di imbarcarsi dall'aeroporto emiliano per Tel Aviv. I secondi sono volati su Catania e da lì, anche loro, hanno tentato di salire a bordo di un volo per la città israeliana. Tutti e quattro sono stati però bloccati, perché scoperti all'imbarco con passaporti israeliani falsi, a poche ore di distanza., I primi due sono stati denunciati a piede libero dalla polizia di frontiera bolognese e poi sono ripartiti in direzione Albania. La donna controllata in Sicilia, secondo quanto si apprende da fonti di sicurezza qualificati, è stata arrestata, il ragazzo rilasciato con una denuncia. Sono in corso accertamenti coordinati delle Digos per comprendere maggiori dettagli su un caso tutto da chiarire, in prossimità dell'anniversario dell'attacco di Hamas del 7 ottobre e pochi giorni dopo il tentativo di dirottamento del FlyDubai., Da quanto si apprende i due intercettati a Bologna non avevano precedenti negli archivi delle forze di polizia e sono risultati regolari sul territorio. Non sono scattati alert specifici in materia di terrorismo, ma è chiaro che le indagini sono solo all'inizio. Erano arrivati in Italia con documenti regolari, del loro paese di origine e con quelli sono saliti sull'aereo per l'Albania. I passaporti falsi sono stati utilizzati per provare a raggiungere Israele., Tra gli aspetti da comprendere è il tipo di legame esistente tra i quattro, dove siano stati nelle ore passate a Bologna, cosa hanno detto quando sono stati bloccati e messi di fronte alla falsità dei documenti esibiti. Del caso bolognese era stata informata anche la Procura che ha aperto un fascicolo e avviato accertamenti, anche se il fatto che l'uomo e la donna siano già nuovamente all'estero rappresenta inevitabilmente una complicazione.
news.summary: Non sono ancora scattati alert specifici in materia di terrorismo
news.author: Tgcom24

news.title: Barge, morto l'ideatore della "Casa che gira": l'abitazione che ruota su se stessa per seguire il sole
news.text: È morto a 91 anni Michele Beltramone, l'artigiano di Barge, nel Cuneese, noto per la "Casa che gira", l'abitazione a forma di fungo che aveva progettato e costruito con le proprie mani e che ruota su se stessa per seguire il sole., Beltramone, non era un ingegnere, né un architetto, ma quello che costruì sulla collina di Barge quarant'anni fa, resta ancora oggi un unicum. Ex artigiano idraulico, con la sola quinta elementare, l'idea della forma a fungo gli venne da un amico geometra, quella della rotazione da un palco circolare per il ballo liscio., Alta circa 8 metri e larga 16, poggia su un cuscinetto di 98 sfere: un motore elettrico da 2 cavalli la porta a un giro completo in 56 minuti, o in 24 ore in base alla velocità che desiderava Beltramone. Per la sua casa era diventato un personaggio su giornali e televisione. A chi in passato gli aveva chiesto il perché di un'abitazione così aveva risposto: "Così sono sempre baciato dal sole". Il funerale sarà celebrato venerdì, 9 ottobre, nella parrocchia di Barge.
news.summary: Lutto nel Cuneese per la scomparsa di Michele Beltramone. Aveva 91 anni
news.author: Tgcom24

news.title: Tutor aziendali, il Cf Aib incontra le imprese: «Accogliere è già educare»
news.text:
Non c’è solo il mestiere da imparare. Per uno studente che entra per la prima volta in un’azienda, il tirocinio significa anche misurarsi con orari, responsabilità, regole e relazioni professionali. È anche per questo che il Centro Formazione AIB ha deciso di incontrare i tutor aziendali che seguono i ragazzi durante i percorsi di tirocinio, un incontro che si è tenuto oggi 7 ottobre.

Un momento di confronto con la direzione e i referenti del Centro, ma anche l’occasione per affrontare alcuni aspetti pratici legati alla gestione dei tirocini, dalla compilazione del registro delle presenze agli altri adempimenti previsti. Al centro resta però il rapporto tra i ragazzi e le persone che li seguono durante l’esperienza in azienda.

Il tutor, infatti, non ha soltanto il compito di trasmettere competenze tecniche: per gli studenti rappresenta anche una figura di riferimento nel primo contatto con il mondo del lavoro. È qui che si inserisce il messaggio scelto dal CF AIB per l’iniziativa: «Accogliere è già educare».

«Accogliere è già educare»

Il tirocinio diventa così il punto di incontro tra ciò che i ragazzi imparano a scuola e la possibilità di sperimentarlo direttamente sul posto di lavoro. «Abbiamo voluto organizzare questi incontri innanzitutto per ringraziare le aziende e i tutor per la disponibilità con cui accolgono i nostri ragazzi e per il tempo che dedicano loro. Vogliamo anche sottolineare quanto sia importante il loro ruolo educativo e condividere gli aspetti organizzativi che fanno parte della gestione dei tirocini. L’incontro di Ome ci ha restituito un riscontro davvero bello, con parole di apprezzamento che ci hanno emozionato: abbiamo trovato grande disponibilità e un sincero interesse a proseguire il dialogo», sottolinea Chiara Musatti, direttrice delle sedi CF AIB di Castel Mella e Ome.

La collaborazione con le imprese rappresenta una componente dei percorsi del CF AIB, scuola di formazione professionale di Fondazione AIB con sedi a Castel Mella e Ome. Oltre ai tirocini, il rapporto con le aziende comprende anche apprendistato e percorsi di specializzazione. L’appuntamento di Castel Mella nasce quindi dall'esigenza di mantenere aperto il confronto tra formazione e imprese, soprattutto nella fase in cui gli studenti iniziano a conoscere concretamente il lavoro e le responsabilità che comporta.
news.author: Redazione Web

news.title: Sicilia, Schifani pensa alle dimissioni dopo la dura telefonata con Tajani. Ma intanto chiede un’altra poltrona garantita
news.text:
Un silenzio assordante avvolge il governatore siciliano Renato Schifani, rinchiuso tra le mura d’orate di Palazzo d’Orleans, in attesa della riunione di giunta attesa per giovedì alle 11. L’ordine del giorno sarà: “Provvedimenti più urgenti”, ma il pensiero sottointeso è: il presidente si dimette, si o no? Le ultime 72 ore hanno scosso l’intero governo regionale, la politica siciliana, gli oppositori e persino gli addetti ai lavori. È iniziato tutto lunedì, quando alla riunione tenutasi a Palermo con i segretari provinciali e quelli delle grandi città di Forza Italia, il commissario regionale e deputato nazionale azzurro Nino Minardo, ha insistito sul tema che serve “un cambio di passo in Sicilia”, perché la “credibilità della politica si difende con il coraggio di cambiare”. Uno schiaffo diretto al governatore, l’ennesimo, arrivato dal suo stesso partito, che già in passato ha messo in risalto le carenze dell’inquilino di Palazzo d’Orleans.
Poche ore più tardi, il governatore interviene tentando di stemperare gli animi: “Le parole di Minardo erano un chiaro riferimento alla situazione vissuta in questi mesi da Forza Italia, con diversi deputati indagati”. Ci sarebbe stata una telefonata tra i due. Crisi rientrata? Macché. Martedì pomeriggio Minardo torna alla carica: “Con Schifani nulla da chiarire”. E aggiunge: “Il cambiamento non è una mia opinione, ma una richiesta che arriva dal partito dopo mesi di ascolto e confronto. È un’esigenza che ho registrato a tutti i livelli di Forza Italia in Sicilia: dai militanti ai consiglieri comunali, dai sindaci ai deputati regionali, fino ai parlamentari. C’è una grande richiesta di cambiamento e, in coscienza, credo che abbiamo il dovere di dare una risposta”. Schifani resta in silenzio per diverse ore, e già si mormora che stesse meditando le dimissioni. Poi il comunicato: “Prendo atto delle dichiarazioni dell’onorevole Minardo. In queste ore sto valutando, con senso di responsabilità, le decisioni da assumere, che comunicherò a breve”.
Sono ore concitate. A tarda serata, il governatore riceve a Palazzo d’Orleans tutto il suo staff, e diversi parlamentari regionali forzisti, tra cui l’assessore alla salute Marcello Caruso. Sarebbero stati presenti anche alcuni onorevoli regionali della maggioranza. Il tema cruciale è: dimissioni? Il governatore avrebbe persino confidato ad una sua persona di fiducia: “Qui noi stiamo affondando”. Poi la telefonata con il segretario nazionale Antonio Tajani, che però non avrebbe sortito le giuste risposte. Secondo quanto ricostruito dal quotidiano La Sicilia, il governatore avrebbe detto a Tajani: “Sono un pezzo di storia di Forza Italia, sono il presidente del consiglio nazionale di Forza Italia, e non mi faccio rottamare da un commissario venuto da un altro partito sei mesi fa”. Il riferimento è a Minardo, che tra il 2019 e il 2025 è stato nella Lega, ricoprendo anche la carica di segretario regionale in Sicilia. Tajani avrebbe rimproverato al governatore di non aver portato a compimento le “tante promesse di cambio di passo”. A Roma ritengono non sia più percorribile la strada per l’eventuale ricandidatura nel 2027. Niente Schifani bis. Il governatore per lasciare vorrebbe un posto garantito: Csm o magari tornare al Senato. La telefonata non rasserena, anzi, lascia molti strascichi.
Il presidente resta in silenzio. Nella mattinata di mercoledì, si presenta al Tribunale di Palermo per partecipare al convegno sull’antimafia. È impassibile, ma teso. Non rilascia nessuna dichiarazione sulla crisi e sull’eventuale possibilità di dimissioni. Solo un breve commento sulla lotta alla illegalità. Nelle stesse ore, torna a parlare Minardo: “Ho proposto nei prossimi giorni un incontro a Roma alla presenza del segretario nazionale di Forza Italia, Antonio Tajani e del Presidente della regione, Renato Schifani. Insieme stabiliremo il percorso politico”. Dopo pranzo la nota da Palazzo d’Orleans con cui si comunica la convocazione della giunta per giovedì mattina.
I malumori e mugugni dei forzisti siciliani si trascinano ormai da anni. Il governatore è accusato di non aver ascoltato “la pancia del partito” e sottovalutato le “difficoltà evidenti” con gli alleati.
In origine è stato Gianfranco Miccichè ad attaccare il governatore (“Schifani è una persona che vive di rancori e delle sue vendette. Non gliene frega niente del bene della Sicilia”), prima che lasciasse FI per fondare con l’ex governatore autonomista Raffaele Lombardo il partito Grande Sicilia. Poi è stata la volta del vicepresidente della Camera, Giorgio Mulè (“In Sicilia Schifani fa troppi errori”) e dell’europarlamentare Marco Falcone (“Schifani sottovaluta il disagio. Un leader non punisce, unisce”). È stata criticata la mancata organizzazione di un congresso regionale e di una struttura definita della segreteria. Per molti il capo espiratorio è stato l’ex coordinamento nell’isola, Marcello Caruso, subentrato nel 2023 a Micciché, troppo vicino a Schifani essendone stato il capo della segreteria particolare quando era al Senato.
Gli attacchi si sono perpetrati nei mesi. Sia Tajani che Maurizio Gasparri, con l’intervento silenzioso di Arcore, hanno tentato di ristabilire la quiete dentro gli azzurri. Schifani ha persino ricevuto il sostegno del presidente del Senato meloniano, Ignazio La Russa, e quella degli altri alleati. Ma la frattura insanabile ha spinto lo scorso aprile a promuovere Caruso al ruolo di responsabile del dipartimento insularità di Forza Italia, e nominare Minardo commissario in Sicilia.
I problemi interni a Forza Italia sono stati amplificati dalle numerose inchieste giudiziarie che hanno colpito il cerchia magico degli “uomini di fiducia” del governatore e dei deputati azzurri. Prima c’è stata l’accusa di concorso esterno in associazione mafiosa per l’ex dirigente generale della pianificazione strategica della salute siciliana e dirigente del Policlinico di Messina, Salvatore Iacolino; nei giorni scorsi quella di corruzione per il presidente della commissione tecnica specialistica (Cts) e consigliere giuridico del governatore, Gaetano Armao. Senza dimenticare gli arresti per corruzione dei deputati regionali forzisti Michele Mancuso e Riccardo Gallo Afflitto.
Anche i componenti della giunta sono stati travolti dalle indagini: corruzione per l’assessore all’agricoltura Luca Sammartino (Lega), associazione a delinquere per l’ex assessore all’energia Roberto Di Mauro (Grande Sicilia) e l’accusa di corruzione per l’assessora al turismo Elvira Amata (Fratelli d’Italia). A questi vanno aggiunti anche il processo per peculato, corruzione e falso per il presidente dell’assemblea regionale Gaetano Galvagno (FdI). E non ultimo, lo scandalo sul leader della nuova Dc ed ex governatore Totò Cuffaro, che ha patteggiato 3 anni ai servizi sociali per corruzione e traffico di influenze; e che vantava un ottimo e saldo rapporto con Schifani, tanto da tessere gli equilibri all’interno del centrodestra.
Sullo sfondo però, resta una situazione delicata sotto l’aspetto della continuità della legislazione. In caso di eventuali dimissioni, la prima finestra utile per andare al voto sarebbe il 13 dicembre e fino a quella data il governo si limiterebbe all’ordinaria amministrazione. Salterebbe quindi la finanziaria, e la regione sarebbe costretta ad operare in esercizio provvisorio. Quindi niente spartizione di fondi e prebende da destinare ai comuni amministrati da politici amici, soprattutto in vista del prossimo voto delle politiche e delle comunali 2027. Inoltre, il voto anticipato costerebbe caro ai deputato regionale che sono al loro primo mandato, perché non maturerebbero la soglia previdenziale prevista dopo 4 anni, 6 mesi e 1 giorni, che scatterebbe solo tra aprile e maggio 2027. Quindi addio alle pensioni d’oro.
news.summary:
Un silenzio assordante avvolge il governatore siciliano Renato Schifani, rinchiuso tra le mura d’orate di Palazzo d’Orleans, in attesa della riunione di giunta attesa per giovedì alle 11. L’ordine del giorno sarà: “Provvedimenti più urgenti”, ma il pensiero sottointeso è: il presidente si dimette, si o no? Le ultime 72 ore hanno scosso l’intero governo […]


L'articolo Sicilia, Schifani pensa alle dimissioni dopo la dura telefonata con Tajani. Ma intanto chiede un’altra poltrona garantita proviene da Il Fatto Quotidiano.
news.author: Saul Caia

news.title: Via Avondo 20, nasce un nuovo spazio culturale: sabato la festa con la raccolta fondi
news.text:
Un punto di riferimento per la creatività e l'incontro tra generazioni diverse. Sabato 10 ottobre, dalle 11 alle 22, l'immobile di via Avondo 20 a Torino aprirà ufficialmente le sue porte per “Fundraising 10 Ottobre”, una maratona di dodici ore pensata per presentare e rilanciare un nuovo spazio culturale pronto a diventare un punto di aggregazione per tutto il quartiere e la città.

Il programma: dalle attività per bambini alle jam session

La giornata prevede un palinsesto ricco e variegato per coinvolgere cittadini di ogni età: si partirà la mattina con sessioni di yoga e meditazione, seguite dal pranzo condiviso e dalla presentazione ufficiale del progetto. Nel corso del pomeriggio spazio alla creatività con workshop di maschere, laboratori di scrittura creativa, attività dedicate ai più piccoli, mercatino e serigrafia, per poi chiudere la serata tra jam session e open consolle.

Una rete per il territorio e la raccolta fondi

L'iniziativa, organizzata dalle realtà promotrici con il coinvolgimento di AICS e il patrocinio della Circoscrizione 6, punta a creare una rete solida capace di sviluppare nuove idee e collaborazioni sul territorio. Durante l'intero evento sarà possibile contribuire con una donazione libera alla raccolta fondi destinata ai lavori di ristrutturazione e allestimento dello spazio, per renderlo sempre più accogliente e funzionale.
